task: Fix the equal per-member budget split (EPMCDME-16072) so small budgets or large member counts never produce negative or inconsistent member spend limits and the sum never exceeds the platform budget, with regression tests.

key_reasoning.reason: The math change is low novelty: replace the HALF_UP share plus last-member remainder in ProjectBudgetService._allocate_equal and _equal_amounts_with_fixed_overrides with one uniform cent-floored share and keep soft <= max. There are non-obvious constraints. EQUAL members share one LiteLLM budget row, and the last member synced wins, so only a uniform value is enforceable. Group category totals can carry sub-cent amounts. Existing lifecycle tests assert the old remainder behaviour. The base score is S. It is bumped to M because the ACs name boundary cases (small budget, large member count) and no boundary-value tests exist for these helpers today.

One component: the static allocation helpers in ProjectBudgetService. They feed the create, group create, category create, resync (update, rebalance, override, clear override) and backfill (BudgetService._create_backfilled_project_budget) paths, plus the shared child budget seeding. The callers pick up the fix without changes. ProjectAssignmentService._get_member_added_allocation_amounts becomes correct once shares are uniform, so at most a test touches it. These are budget-domain helpers, not core shared utilities, so no scope bump applies.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from S to M: the ACs list edge cases (70 members / $1, sum <= budget, small budgets and large member counts) and no boundary-value test template exists. _allocate_equal has zero direct tests.
